parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a strongly protective division (public-accommodations, hate-crime, shield laws, gender-neutral single-user restrooms) nested inside a hostile federal layer. Universal exposures persist despite local law: the Feb 2025 visa cable directs refusal on any document/sex discrepancy and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers halted; federal orders bar trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities. Worst documented chain is federal custody — immigration detainees report beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; corrections policy mandates haircuts, hormone removal, conversion-style therapy — a tier-2 state-tolerated targeting exposure. Several orders are enjoined, litigation pending, and division recourse machinery exists but lacks enforcement data. Local protections lift it above the 0.45 tier; federal facility exclusion plus custody abuse hold it below 0.55-B.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tells posts to refuse any case with document/sex discrepancy or doubt about sex, and to weigh fraud-based permanent ineligibility; X-marker passports halted; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated. Universal visa-stage exposure for trans applicants.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; pre-2025 X passports valid to expiry; legal-aid FAQ; ACLU suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Adjudication at an overseas post feeds the entry decision; division equality law cannot touch federal visa or passport processing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans immigration detainees report forced labour with gendered justifications, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal, substitute psychiatric drugs); trans prisoner counts suppressed since 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; litigation ongoing; earlier prison LGBTQ-rights order only rescinded, not replaced by statute.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy → secondary inspection → investigation → federal custody, where birth-sex placement and the conversion-style policy apply; division protections do not reach federal detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity nationwide, including federal buildings inside this division; 19 divisions restrict facilities, 4 criminalise in certain circumstances, one documented 2025 trespass arrest (held 24h in men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no mapped ban, requires gender-neutral single-user restrooms since 2018, and its public-accommodations law covers hotels, restaurants, shops and services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule operates inside the division; local law does not preempt it, so airports and federal sites remain exposure.

care_services.exposure: Federal funding freeze, DOJ subpoenas of under-19 hospital records including names and notes, proposed public-insurance bar for trans under-18s; 27 divisions ban youth gender care.
care_services.protection: Division shield laws (2023, 2024) enforceable against out-of-state civil/criminal action; insurance coverage mandate since 2013; conversion therapy on minors prohibited.
care_services.interaction: A visiting family's care-seeking can travel into federal subpoena and funding machinery; shield laws protect within the division but not federal records demands.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 reward memo cites 'radical gender ideology' among extremist framings; EO directs law-enforcement investigation of schools promoting 'gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo never makes gender ideology a reward criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; gender-identity hate crimes punishable nationally; division repealed the panic defence (2021).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises the temperature of any police encounter even where division officers are protective.

minors_guardians.exposure: EOs label youth gender care 'mutilation', direct criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, and authorise under-19 record subpoenas; October 2025 proposed rule blocks loan forgiveness for providers of youth care.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield laws, anti-bullying law covering gender identity, 2023 education-department policy protecting trans students; several EOs enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting minor's school-facing exposure is resident-sphere, but care, records and facility rules reach the travelling family wherever federal authority operates.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Only 23 divisions cover gender identity in bias statutes; 2025 polling shows 66% support ASAB on government documents and 69% support sex-aligned athletics — indicating a substantial disapproving public minority.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime penalty for gender identity (1999), public-accommodations and housing protections, panic defence abolished; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Division law governs street assault response, but no enforcement data is sourced, so operation of these protections is unverified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state-specific enforcement data for hate-crime or public-accommodations complaints; shield-law provisions not itemised; national posture shifts as orders are enjoined or allowed (passport rule took effect Nov 2025), so exposure is time-of-travel dependent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ, equality and identity-document trackers, pending ACLU litigation, four divisions flagged Do Not Travel (this one is not), division in the most-protective tier as of July 2026.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal remedies are slow and agency-controlled; division remedies are unused on this record.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars trans visitors wholesale with unpublished criteria and no remedy. This jurisdiction's visa cable refuses only on documented discrepancy/doubt, fraud findings are non-automatic with limited waiver, and litigation plus a legal-aid FAQ exist; entry exclusion is narrower and contestable, so higher than 0.35.

Vesskar shows universal document-exposure at routine checkpoints, documented detention and denial of care with scarce legal aid. Comparable universal document exposure here, but this division's operative public-accommodations, hate-crime and shield protections materially reduce everyday and service risk, so somewhat higher.

Kestrel Isles: secondary screening, administrative refusal, slow appeals, no custody harm. This dossier matches that entry profile but adds documented federal custody abuse (beatings, sexual abuse, solitary) and a nationwide federal facility exclusion — worse than 0.55-B.

Meridia has trained border staff, brief detention with counsel, compensation for unlawful holding, low severity. Here officers are instructed to refuse on discrepancy, custody abuse is documented, and federal facility rules apply — clearly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The division itself operates a protective regime — public-accommodations coverage of hotels and services, gender-identity hate-crime penalties, abolished panic defence, gender-neutral single-user restrooms, shield laws enforceable against out-of-state action — genuinely mitigating street, service and in-division care exposure. But V3 requires rating the combined regime: federal authority supplies the sharpest exposures, and division law cannot preempt them. Visa adjudication with discrepancy-based refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, the end of X markers, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities, and documented abuses in federal immigration and corrections custody all follow the traveller regardless of locale. Litigation is genuinely unresolved, cutting both ways: some orders are enjoined, others (passport rules) are in force. Net: meaningful local protection inside a nationally hostile, partially enforced federal layer.
